chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Hudhayl ibn Sadah al-Tahhan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys goods or a garment, takes it to his house, and has not yet paid anything, then it becomes pleasing to him (or he likes it), so he returns it. Is it permissible for him to do so? He said, 'No, unless the owner is pleased with it.'

key_terms.فَيَبْدُو لَهُ: it becomes pleasing to him / he likes it

ai.seo_question: Can a buyer return goods before paying for them?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the right to return goods purchased on credit is not unilateral but contingent upon the seller's consent, emphasizing the principle of mutual agreement (*taradi*) in commercial transactions. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on preserving the seller's goodwill and preventing unilateral disruption of the contract, distinguishing it from absolute rights of return found in other contexts.
